Correct me if I'm wrong, but as far as I see from code, this is expected behavior:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/core/src/linker/view_container_ref.ts#L139-L145

So you have to destroy viewRef calling `destroy` instead of `detach`

> Correct me if I'm wrong, but as far as I see from code, this is expected behavior:
> So you have to destroy viewRef calling `destroy` instead of `detach`

I'm not really talking about destroying a `ViewRef`. Anytime a `ViewRef` is removed from a `ViewRefContainer` (other than using `viewRef.destroy()`), `viewRef._viewContainerRef ` still points to that `ViewRefContainer` instance. Therefore that `ViewRefContainer` will never be garbage collected until the `ViewRef` instance is attached to another container or its `destroy` method is called.

# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/core ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: Pre-Ivy or if you disable Ivy ### Description **Problem: ComponentRef.onDestroyed callback does not get called** A component gets dynamically created via `ComponentFactoryResolver`. It is then inserted into the view. ```typescript @ViewChild("anchor", { read: ViewContainerRef }) anchor: ViewContainerRef; ``` ```typescript this.compRef = this.cfr .resolveComponentFactory(DynamicComponent) .create(this.injector); this.compRef.onDestroy(() => console.log("DynamicComponent onDestroyed callback") ); this.anchor.insert(this.compRef.hostView); ``` As you can see, the `onDestroyed` callback is attached. If the component gets destroyed by its ComponentRef, the callback **gets called correctly** like so: ```typescript this.compRef.destroy(); ``` if the component gets destroyed by clearing the `anchor`, the callback **does not get called**: ```typescript this.anchor.clear(); ``` As far as I can tell, the `onDestroyed` callback **ONLY** gets called when the component gets destroyed by its `ComponentRef`. Whenever the component gets destroyed by clearing parent views or navigating away or data binding, the callback does not get called. It works in NG 8.2.14 and it works if you set `enableIvy: false` in tsconfig.json. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-ev4v2y](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-ev4v2y) ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:**

body:
Looked at this with @mhevery, sounds like a legitimate bug. Summary is:
* `ViewRef._viewContainerRef` references a `ViewContainerRef` 
* This property is never cleared when the `ViewRef` is _detached_ from that `ViewContainerRef`
* Unclear if this property is unset when the `ViewContainerRef` is destroyed

issue.title: fix(core): memory leak if view container host view is destroyed while view ref is not
issue.body:
When we attach a `ViewRef` to a `ViewContainerRef`, we save a reference to the container onto the `ViewRef` so that we can remove it when the ref is destroyed. The problem is that if the container's `hostView` is destroyed first, the `ViewRef` has no way of knowing that it should stop referencing the container.

These changes remove the leak by not saving a reference at all. Instead, when a `ViewRef` is destroyed, we clean it up through the `LContainer` directly. We don't need to worry about the case where the container is destroyed before the view, because containers automatically clean up all of their views upon destruction.

Fixes #38648.
